blind_reader_rulings.reason: The „rotes Brot“ quoting at first running-text occurrence (ix.heroSum) with no quotes thereafter (ix.bakeriesH/ix.bakeriesNote) is the deliberate gloss_regel convention (glossed/marked once per term per page), matching the published /de/food/ dish-card precedent ('Auch als „rotes Brot“ (khubz ahmar) bekannt'). It is not an accidental inconsistency. Rewriting to 'Bäckereien, die rotes Brot backen' would also break the parallel construction ix.bakeriesH already establishes on this same page. No fact changed either way, so this is a stylistic preference against a sourced convention, not a defect.

Valid clarity issue: en/ar both structure this as 'from A and B to C and D' (two axes — setting and food/drink — folded into one span), which the German reproduced literally and which does read as one confusing scale. Restructured into two clearly paired clauses (setting axis, then food/drink axis) with no fact added or removed and 'traditional' kept attached to Hausmannskost exactly as in en/ar ('traditional food').

Rewritten to attach the click directly to the location, preserving both facts (has a photo; the location is one click away in Google Maps) without adding or dropping anything.

blind_reader_rulings.reason: 'stetig' is not filler doubling 'weiter': per Stage 4's fact-fence audit, 'stetig' carries ar's تباعاً (successively/gradually), a nuance en's plain 'keeps growing' does not state explicitly, while 'wächst weiter' is the idiomatic rendering of en's 'keeps growing' itself. Dropping either word would drop a fact tied to one of the two sources. The site-wide repetition the observation also flags spans a third occurrence in the 'Über diese Seite' method box (ix.methodH/P1), which is out of this batch's scope (de-din-2).

'Tafeln' was deliberately chosen at Stage 4 to match the published /de/food/ sibling ('Von der Oasentafel') and to carry en's 'tables'/ar's موائد figurative sense (a spread, hospitality, cuisine) rather than bare furniture. The suggested replacement 'Essen und Trinken in Al-Ahsa' is safer but flattens that register and drops the figurative image both source texts carry. A momentary first-read ambiguity (chalkboard vs. dining table) is resolved immediately by the following H1 'Restaurants und Cafés' and is not enough to discard a wording already established as the site's convention for this figure.

termbase_additions_final.source: Web-verified (Stage 4, 2026-09-19): masculine confirmed two ways — (1) the compound's Grundwort „Kaffee“ is masculine (germanwithlaura.com/kaffee/: „'Kaffee' is der: der Kaffee (the coffee)“), and German compounds take the gender of their final element; (2) attested apposition in running industry text at roastmarket.de/magazin/der-specialty-coffee/: „Der Begriff Spezialitätenkaffee ist zwar kein geschützter Begriff wie etwa Fairtrade“. Term additionally corroborated as the German coffee trade's stable rendering of „specialty coffee“ by coffeeness.de/specialty-coffee/, cafesito.de/blog/spezialitaeten-kaffee/ and Deutscher Kaffeeverband e. V. usage (kaffeeverband.de).

tm_pairs.en: Your guide to dining in Al Ahsa: hand-picked restaurants, cafés and red-bread bakeries across Hofuf, Al-Mubarraz and beyond — from heritage settings and traditional food to modern spots and specialty coffee — each with its photo and its place on Google Maps, one tap away. The list keeps growing.

notes:
Batch de-din-1 (index frame of /de/restaurants-cafes/: hero, section headings, card UI, search/filter/counter, Google Maps notes) approved at 94/100. Two genuine clarity/nativeness fixes applied to ix.heroSum from the blind reader (the 'von A/B bis C/D' single-scale confusion split into two clearly paired clauses; the dangling 'einen Klick entfernt' reattached directly to the location) and one to ix.hoursNote ('prüfen Sie sie' euphony). One observation (18, ix.openNow/ix.openFilter sharing 'Jetzt geöffnet') is a source_defect: en/ar use the identical string for both a status badge and a filter toggle, so the German stays faithful rather than inventing a distinction the source does not make. Eight observations (10-17, all FAQ) and one district-name observation (6, plus part of 15) belong to the parallel de-din-2 batch and were not ruled on their merits here, per the judge brief's explicit routing. Two observations (8, 9) concern published/structural or LOCKED elements outside this batch and were rejected on that basis alone, with no factual error found in either. Three observations (1, 5, 7) were rejected because the flagged wording is a deliberate, sourced choice (gloss_regel first-occurrence quoting; matching the published /de/food/ 'Oasentafel' register and figurative sense; matching the published /de/stay/ 'Die erste Gruppe' sibling for cross-page consistency) rather than a defect. One observation (4) was rejected because the 'redundant' words each carry a distinct fact tied to en ('keeps growing') and ar (تباعاً / successively) respectively.
BINDING: ix.newWindow / ix.ratingLabel / ix.closedPerm / ix.closedTemp stay locked verbatim in every future dining page (card batches ج6 3-5 and the restaurant single pages ج7) — do not resynonymize or reformat.
BINDING: 'der Spezialitätenkaffee' (specialty coffee) is now termbase-final with a verified gender witness — reuse verbatim in card batches and single pages; do not substitute 'Spezialitätskaffee' or any other variant.
BINDING: ix.openNow and ix.openFilter are identically worded ('Jetzt geöffnet') by design, mirroring identical en/ar source text for both uses — this is a source-level fact (logged as source_defect, not fixed), and any future page reusing this status badge or filter toggle must keep them identical rather than trying to differentiate the wording.
BINDING: the C5b pair 'rotes Brot' / 'Dattelbrot' is satisfied on the index page via ix.heroSum (quoted at first running-text mention) + ix.bakeriesNote (names Dattelbrot) — any dining single page for one of the four bakeries must independently carry both terms on its own page (C5b is a per-page guard).
BINDING: the Tanur gloss '(Lehmofen)' is used exactly once, at the first running-text occurrence, and only in running text (never in a heading/eyebrow) — ix.bakeriesEyebrow stays unglossed by design; any bakery single page introducing 'Tanur' in its own running text needs its own first-occurrence gloss, since gloss_regel scope is per page.
BINDING: ix.listEyebrow 'Die erste Gruppe' and ix.moreLabel 'Details zum Ort' match the published /de/stay/ siblings verbatim, and ix.title 'Restaurants und Cafés' matches published nav.dine verbatim — card batches and single pages must not introduce alternate wording for these same UI concepts.
BINDING: self-designated Latin venue names (e.g. 'Al-Koot Heritage Hotel & Restaurant', '7st. Speciality Coffee') must always be reproduced in full exactly as the venue spells itself wherever they appear in prose (FAQ, single-page body text) — never abbreviated or partially quoted; this was flagged as a live defect risk to the de-din-2 judge and applies equally to ج7 single pages.
BINDING: district/area names on dining content (Al-Koot-Viertel, Al-Rifaa-Nord-Viertel, Al-Mazrou' with its ʻayn mark, etc.) are the de-din-2 judge's responsibility via districts.ts — card batches (ج6 3-5) and single pages (ج7) using area_de on individual venues should not publish ahead of that judge's final district naming to avoid drift.
